decisions.reason: SAP page 9 restricts Completers to the efficacy population, while Define-XML ADSL.COMP24FL requires only visit 12 and ENDDT on or after that visit. The efficacy-population condition is absent from the Define-XML rule.

Define-XML ADSL.BMIBL multiplies HEIGHTBL by 100, and the literal probe's _BMIBL_RAW and BMIBL state that formula with one-decimal rounding, so the near-zero observed values follow from it. The metres reading rests on the kg/m^2 label of ADSL.BMIBL and the cm label of ADSL.HEIGHTBL, and adsl_v1.yaml BMIBL_RAW likewise divides height by 100.

Define-XML ADSL.BMIBLGR1 explicitly assigns Obese when BMIBL >=30, matching SAP page 13. BMICAT's '>30' is the stored code for Obese, so comparing that code with the SAP's numeric condition does not establish a conflicting boundary rule; the code-conformance issue is covered by CR-9.

Define-XML ADSL.BMIBLGR1 explicitly assigns Obese when BMIBL >=30, matching the obese(>=30) condition on SAP page 22. BMICAT's '>30 = Obese' names a category code rather than replacing that derivation condition, so this comparison does not establish contradictory numeric grouping rules.

The literal probe keeps the '. < BMIBL' exclusion of a missing BMI in Define-XML ADSL.BMIBLGR1 and stores Obese as the BMICAT code '>30', so the code differences and the ungrouped missing-BMI subject follow from the documented rule. The '>=30' reading of SAP pages 13 and 22 removes only the code differences, leaving the subject whose missing BMI the reference and adsl_v1.yaml BMIBLGR1 place in '<25'.

The BMICAT codelist attached to Define-XML ADSL.BMIBLGR1 enumerates '<25', '25-<30', and '>30', while the report records '>=30' in both outputs. No value-level qualification in that section exempts these BMI-group records from the codelist.

Define-XML ADSL.EDUCLVL names SC.SCSTRESN for SCTESTCD=YEARSEDU, and the probe's SC_YEARSEDU filter states it literally, so every result is missing where the reference has a value. The EDLEVEL reading, which adsl_v1.yaml SC_EDU also uses, reproduces the reference, though it rests on the staged SC test code rather than a document statement.

SAP page 13 measures disease duration to Week -2 (Visit 1), while page 22 measures it to enrollment. SAP page 9 identifies enrollment with treatment assignment at Week 0 (Visit 3), so the endpoints differ.

The full Define-XML ADSL.VISNUMEN comment restricts both branches to DSTERM='PROTCOL COMPLETED', whereas its label includes early termination. The completion-only source condition does not implement the label's early-termination scope.

Define-XML ADSL.VISNUMEN supplies a visit only from a completion record, while SAP page 10 defines end of treatment to include the early termination visit. Correcting the spelling of PROTCOL would not remove that scope difference.

The literal probe keeps the DSTERM='PROTCOL COMPLETED' condition of Define-XML ADSL.VISNUMEN, which no record matches, so every result is missing. The readings correct that spelling and then apply the end of treatment of SAP pages 10, 17 and 40-42, and the reported results follow each change, with only the last-visit-on-or-before-Week-24 reading reproducing the reference.

SAP page 10 pools sites by a condition on enrollment within each treatment group, while adsl_v1.yaml SITEGR1 lists fixed SITEID values. The list is the rule's result on this data rather than the condition, and no specification element computes enrollment counts.

SAP page 10 adds a second step that combines a still-short pooled group with the next fewest-enrolling site. The fixed list in adsl_v1.yaml SITEGR1 is the only pooling logic, and neither it nor the entry adsl.yaml, which adds only Define-XML metadata, states that step.
SAP page 10 breaks a tie for fewest-enrolling site with a random-number generator. No element of adsl_v1.yaml or the entry adsl.yaml states a tie condition or a random selection.

Define-XML ADSL.TRTSDT explicitly selects SV.SVSTDTC at VISITNUM=3, whereas EX_MINDTC selects MIN(EX.EXSTDTC). A minimum exposure-start date is a different source and selection from the specified visit record.

SAP page 16 defines the reference as the date of first dose and qualifies Week 0 (Visit 3) with 'unless indicated otherwise'. EX_MINDTC's earliest exposure start expresses the first-dose concept, so this SAP quote does not require a fixed visit-3 source; the separate Define-XML source difference remains.

Define-XML ADSL.TRTEDT allows the discontinuation-date fallback only when the subject discontinued after visit 3. adsl_v1.yaml TRTEDT takes DS_DISP.DSSTDTC whenever LAST_EXENDTC is missing, and DS_DISP filters only on DSCAT, so no element states the visit-3 condition.
Define-XML ADSL.CUMDOSE multiplies TRT01PN by TRTDUR for its specified lower-dose branches. CUMDOSE_BASE instead sums actual EX doses over EX study-day intervals, a different source computation.

Define-XML ADSL.CUMDOSE specifies the high-dose titration amounts and visit-4/visit-12 interval boundaries. CUMDOSE_BASE and the remaining dose helpers sum EX records without implementing those documented visit-boundary branches.

Define-XML ADSL.AGEGR1N and its codelist pair each AGE cutpoint one-to-one with an AGEGR1 group, so deriving AGEGR1 from AGE with those cutpoints, as adsl_v1.yaml AGEGR1 does, gives the group that decoding AGEGR1N gives. The reversed order of the two derivations restates the same categorization rather than a different condition, source or computation.

adsl_v1.yaml AGEGR1 tests the AGE cutpoints of Define-XML ADSL.AGEGR1N, with 65 and 80 in the middle group, and AGEGR1N maps those groups to the codelist codes 1, 2 and 3. Composed, the specification states the documented conditions and codes, using the character group only as an intermediate.

Define-XML ADSL.RACEN codes ASIAN as 7, and ADSL.RACE lists ASIAN among its values. The adsl_v1.yaml RACEN mapping has no ASIAN entry, and the entry's RACEN codelist reference is Define-XML metadata rather than a derivation, so an ASIAN subject would get a missing RACEN.

Define-XML ADSL.BMIBL multiplies HEIGHTBL by 100 in the denominator, while BMIBL_RAW divides HEIGHTBL by 100. These are different computations even though the specification's conversion is appropriate for the documented centimetre units.
In Define-XML ADSL.BMIBLGR1, '. < BMIBL <25' is false for a missing BMI, so a subject without baseline BMI falls in no group. adsl_v1.yaml BMIBLGR1 explicitly assigns a missing BMIBL to '<25'.

SAP page 10 says missing baseline values will not be imputed. adsl_v1.yaml BMIBLGR1 assigns '<25' to a missing BMIBL, supplying a baseline BMI group where the documented rule groups only a nonmissing BMI.
Define-XML ADSL.HEIGHTBL and SAP page 13 require visit-1 height. BASE_HT selects the earliest HEIGHT record by VISITNUM without restricting it to visit 1, so it can select a different visit.
Define-XML ADSL.WEIGHTBL and SAP page 13 specify visit-3 weight. BASE_WT instead selects VSBLFL='Y' without the VISITNUM=3 condition, and no retained section equates those selection predicates.
Define-XML ADSL.EDUCLVL selects SCTESTCD=YEARSEDU. SC_EDU selects EDLEVEL, so the documented and implemented test-code sources differ.
Define-XML ADSL.VISNUMEN restricts the source to DSTERM='PROTCOL COMPLETED'. DS_DISP and VISNUMEN use disposition-event records without that completion condition.

Define-XML ADSL.MMSETOT sums the original result QS.QSORRES, while adsl_v1.yaml MMSETOT sums QS.QSSTRESN. No retained section states that the standardized numeric result replaces QSORRES for this total.

SAP page 10 describes the MMSE covariate as baseline disease severity, and page 13 compares MMSE at baseline. adsl_v1.yaml MMSETOT and QS_MMSE filter only on QSCAT, and no specification element restricts the MMSE records to a baseline visit or assessment.

Define-XML ADSL.TRTSDT calls only for conversion to a SAS date, while adsl_v1.yaml TRTSDT completes a partial date with month 1 and day 1. The retained sections state partial-date imputation only for adverse event start dates (Define-XML ADAE.ASTDT, SAP page 16, data guide page 5), not for treatment start.

Define-XML ADSL.TRTEDT states the source, a conditional fallback and conversion to a SAS date, without partial-date completion. adsl_v1.yaml TRTEDT completes both sources with month 1 and day 1, and the only imputation rules in the retained sections concern adverse event start dates.

Define-XML ADSL.AVGDD states CUMDOSE/TRTDUR, whose SAS result is missing when TRTDUR is zero. AVGDD_RAW's NULLIF(TRTDUR, 0) preserves that undefined-division result and adds no distinct substantive condition to the documented computation.

adsl_v1.yaml CUMDOSE adds _DOSE0 times _DAYS0, which extends a last EX record without an end date to TRTEDT through LAST_EX_DAYS. Define-XML ADSL.CUMDOSE computes planned doses over visit intervals and SAP pages 10, 15 and 31 define the end of study, but no retained section mentions EX records or this extension.
Define-XML ADSL.DISONSDT converts the primary-diagnosis MHSTDTC to a SAS date without imputation. No retained section states the month 1 and day 1 completion in adsl_v1.yaml DISONSDT.
Define-XML ADSL.DURDIS and SAP pages 13 and 22 state the duration in months without a conversion rule. No retained section states the 30.4375-day divisor in adsl_v1.yaml DURDIS.

Define-XML ADSL.DURDIS and SAP pages 13 and 22 state months between dates without an inclusive day-count rule; no retained section supplies one. adsl.yaml lines 1099-1100 explicitly count both endpoint days before conversion to months.

Define-XML ADSL.DURDIS and SAP pages 13 and 22 give no month convention, partial-month treatment or interval inclusivity, and no other retained section supplies one. SAP page 22 also measures to enrollment, which page 9 places at visit 3, while Define-XML and page 13 use visit 1, so no unique literal probe can be stated.
Define-XML ADSL.VISIT1DT converts the visit-1 SVSTDTC to a SAS date without imputation. No retained section states the month 1 and day 1 completion in adsl_v1.yaml VISIT1DT.
Define-XML ADSL.RFENDT converts RFENDTC to a SAS date without imputation. No retained section states the month 1 and day 1 completion in adsl_v1.yaml RFENDT.

Define-XML ADSL.DCREASCD describes grouping and lists DISCREAS outputs, but neither it nor ADSL.DCDECOD pairs the different source and output terms. SAP page 21 supplies display categories and a lack-of-efficacy footnote, while the full retained-section search found no mapping for the DC_REAS_MAP pairs.

Define-XML ADSL.DCREASCD lists I/E Not Met and SAP page 21 displays Protocol criteria not met, but neither names a DSTERM source. No retained section states the DSTERM = 'PROTOCOL ENTRY CRITERIA NOT MET' condition in adsl_v1.yaml DCREASCD.

Define-XML ADSL.DCREASCD calls the variable a grouping of DCDECOD values and lists the DISCREAS groups, but pairs no DCDECOD value with a group and names no source for I/E Not Met. SAP page 21 gives display categories only, so the grouping cannot be stated as a probe without choosing the mapping.

Define-XML ADSL.MMSETOT sums QS.QSORRES for the subject without naming the contributing questionnaire records or how textual results become numbers. SAP pages 10 and 13 add only that the MMSE is a baseline measure, so the rule cannot be stated as a probe without added choices.
